Must possess valid California Driver's License to drive a County or University vehicle. Ability and means to travel on a flexible schedule as needed, proof of liability damage insurance on vehicle used is required. Reimbursement of job-related travel will be reimbursed according to University policies.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

The University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC ANR) invites applications for an Industry Alliances Specialist 2 to serve as the Ecosystem and Community Engagement Coordinator for UC ANR Innovate. The position helps build and maintain connections among industry, researchers, entrepreneurs, growers, food producers, and innovation organizations while coordinating UC ANR’s activities under the CAPBIO Ecosystem project.
Program Communications and Online Engagement

The incumbent coordinates CAPBIO Connect opportunities that bring selected early-stage companies together with potential end users to showcase technologies and gather feedback. The incumbent also coordinates CAPBIO Build workshops that help researchers and entrepreneurs explore customer needs, product-market fit, and early-stage validation. This work includes participant intake, scheduling, partner and service-provider coordination, follow-up, and tracking of activities, expenses, milestones, and outcomes. The position supports related partner engagement and develops social media and online communications to recruit participants, maintain connections, and share program opportunities and results.

Uses social media and online channels to identify and engage prospective program participants and partners, promote opportunities, and maintain connections across  UC ANR Innovate’s innovation ecosystem, in particular the CA AG Tech Alliance. .

Under general direction, the incumbent manages assignments of moderate scope and complexity, exercises judgment within established guidelines, and works with program leadership and the communications lead to ensure accurate, timely delivery of activities, communications, and grant reporting
Develops and maintains an editorial calendar aligned with program activities, recruitment needs, events, partner announcements, and grant deliverables.

UC ANR Innovate is a statewide program of UC ANR that advances applied innovation across agriculture, food systems, and biotechnology in California. The program manages and supports a portfolio of initiatives focused on technology commercialization, workforce development, and regional innovation ecosystems, working closely with researchers, growers, startups, industry partners, and public agencies to coordinate programs, events, funding activities, and communications that support real-world adoption and measurable outcomes. Its current portfolio includes the CA AG Tech Alliance and CAPBIO, which are grant-funded, multi-partner initiatives to grow California’s agri-, food-, and bioeconomy and ecosystem.

Writes, schedules, and publishes content tailored to each platform and audience, including LinkedIn and Instagram. Adapts articles, videos, program announcements, and partner stories into engaging social content.
This position is a career appointment that is 100% fixed and ends on January 31, 2028 with the possibility of extension if funding permits.

Builds relationships with relevant organizations and individuals, amplifies partner content, and encourages participation. Monitors comments and messages, responds to routine inquiries, and brings sensitive issues and emerging opportunities to the communications lead.

This position may be eligible for a hybrid work arrangement, combining remote work with on-site work at the designated office in Davis, CA. Candidates must be available to work on-site at least two days per week, with additional on-site work and travel as business needs require.

Works closely with the communications lead on messaging and campaign priorities and with creative staff on graphics, photography, video, and other visual assets. Coordinates timelines and approvals and manages routine publishing independently within established guidelines.
Pay Scale: $33.44/hour to $46.46/hour
Tracks channel performance, audience growth, engagement, and contributions to program objectives.
Job Posting Close Date: This job is open until filled. The first application review date will be 12/9/2026.
CAPBIO Build and Connect Coordination
Schedules, participant communications, partner coordination, deliverables, and follow-up.
Identifies and recruits early-stage companies for CAPBIO Connect and manages intake and selection logistics in coordination with program leadership and partners.
Organizes opportunities for selected companies to showcase their technologies and receive feedback from potential end users, including growers, food producers, and other biotechnology users.
Coordinates CAPBIO Build cohort and  workshops for researchers and entrepreneurs focused on product-market fit, customer discovery, and early-stage validation.
Identifies and coordinates speakers, facilitators, contractors, and other service providers needed to deliver Connect and Build activities.
Builds relationships with existing innovation and entrepreneurship organizations in the Greater Sacramento region to support recruitment, referrals, and coordinated program delivery.

Tracks participation, feedback, expenses, milestones, and outcomes; maintains project records and prepares materials for grant progress reports. Coordinates UC ANR’s CAPBIO Connect and Build activities.
CAPBIO Ecosystem Project Coordination & Reporting

Coordinates and implements projects and activities to deliver UC ANR’s scope of work under the CAPBIO Ecosystem project, tracking tasks, timelines, and deliverables across UC ANR staff and project partners and communicating status to the project lead.

Compiles and prepares periodic grant progress reports, metrics, narratives, and supporting documentation on ecosystem growth, partner engagement, and communications reach for submission to the project lead, UC ANR, and the funder.

Maintains organized project records, including partner agreements, meeting notes, deliverable trackers, and performance data; supports project and partner meetings by scheduling, preparing agendas, taking notes, and following up on action items.

Assists in identifying gaps in ecosystem program services and proposes ideas to better meet partner needs; implements approved program improvements and keeps related staff and partners updated to maintain consistency.
General Program Support and Other Duties as Assigned
Provides occasional event support for UC ANR Innovate, Alliance, and CAPBIO convenings in coordination with ANR event staff and program managers.

Provides occasional administrative support to the industry alliance program, such as maintaining contact and distribution lists, responding to routine partner inquiries, and referring partner questions to the appropriate program manager.
Performs additional duties as assigned to support UC ANR Innovate.

Acquiring knowledge about University and industry research pertaining to the specific industry alliance program, including UC ANR research and programs in agriculture, food systems, biotechnology, and the bioeconomy.

Solid communication skills, including verbal, written, and active listening; ability to write clear, concise, engaging content and adapt messaging for different platforms and audiences. Natural political acumen and social perceptiveness.

Demonstrated interpersonal skills. Ability to develop working relationships within the department, among campus and UC ANR research staff, and with industry and community partners and online communities. Demonstrated customer service orientation.

Proven organizational skills and the ability to manage time effectively and prioritize tasks across multiple projects and deadlines. Takes initiative and works independently with direction and oversight.

Ability to perform all commonly applicable functions in word processing and spreadsheet software (Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace). Ability to use software applications specific to the industry alliance program, including social media management and scheduling tools, native platform analytics, project tracking, and contact-management tools.
Ability to break down moderately complex concepts and communicate them in an understandable way to technical and non-technical audiences.

Demonstrated experience managing social media channels for an organization or program, including LinkedIn and Instagram: developing editorial calendars, writing and scheduling platform-specific content, monitoring and engaging with online communities, and applying brand, tone, and accessibility guidelines.

Ability to track and interpret channel performance, audience growth, and engagement metrics, and to compile and accurately report performance, expenses, and project status for management and grant reporting.
Demonstrated attention to detail and ability to handle sensitive or proprietary partner information with discretion.
At least two (2) years of experience supporting communications, marketing, partnership, or program coordination functions in a professional environment.
Experience supporting grant-funded, multi-program, university, or public-sector initiatives, including preparing progress reports or tracking deliverables and budgets.
Experience adapting existing visual assets or producing simple graphics and short-form video for social channels using tools such as Canva, Adobe Express, or comparable software.
Experience providing social media coverage of events, including live or near-live posting and on-site content capture.
Familiarity with social media management platforms (e.g., Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Buffer) and website content management systems (e.g., WordPress).
Experience preparing analytics summaries or dashboards using platform insights or tools such as Google Analytics, and experience guiding interns or student assistants.
Interest or background in agriculture, food systems, biotechnology, biomanufacturing, or innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystems.
Spanish or other second-language proficiency.
Special Conditions of Employment:
Occasional evening or weekend availability based on event schedules.

As of January 1, 2014, ANR is a smoke- and tobacco-free environment in which smoking, the use of smokeless tobacco products, and the use of unregulated nicotine products (e-cigarettes), is strictly prohibited.

“Misconduct” means any violation of the policies governing employee conduct at the applicant’s previous place of employment, including, but not limited to, violations of policies prohibiting sexual harassment, sexual assault, or other forms of harassment, or discrimination, as defined by the employer. For reference, below are UC’s policies addressing some forms of misconduct:
UC Sexual Violence and Sexual Harassment Policy
UC Anti-Discrimination Policy
Abusive Conduct in the Workplace
It is the policy of the University of California to undertake affirmative action and anti-discrimination efforts, consistent with its obligations as a Federal and State contractor.

The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check. This is a designated position requiring a background check and may require fingerprinting due to the nature of the job responsibilities. UC ANR does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities.

As a condition of employment, you will be required to comply with the University of California Policy on Vaccination Programs, as may be amended or revised from time to time.  Federal, state, or local public health directives may impose additional requirements.

Misconduct Disclosure Requirement: As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
